title_en: Oil embargo and the 1973–74 bear market
description_en: On 19 October 1973, immediately after President Nixon asked Congress for emergency aid to Israel in the Yom Kippur War, the Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) instituted an oil embargo on the United States; the embargo stopped US oil imports from participating OAPEC nations and began a series of production cuts that altered the world price of oil.
source_title: Federal Reserve History: Oil Shock of 1973-74

description_en: On the evening of 6 October 1979 Fed Chairman Paul Volcker announced that the Federal Open Market Committee would shift its focus to managing the volume of bank reserves instead of the day-to-day level of the federal funds rate, an approach that would lead to more fluctuation in rates and, Volcker hoped, rein in inflation.
source_title: Federal Reserve History: Volcker's Announcement of Anti-Inflation Measures

description_en: On 19 October 1987, a day known as Black Monday, a chain reaction of market distress sent global stock exchanges plummeting in a matter of hours; in the United States, the Dow Jones Industrial Average's fall in a single trading session remains the largest one-day stock market decline in history.
source_title: Federal Reserve History: Stock Market Crash of 1987

description_en: On 2 August 1990 Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait and overran the country in a matter of hours; the invasion led to a United Nations Security Council embargo and sanctions on Iraq and to a U.S.-led coalition air and ground war that began on 16 January 1991.
source_title: Office of the Historian: Gulf War, 1991

description_en: On 4 February 1994 Chairman Alan Greenspan announced that the Federal Open Market Committee had decided to increase slightly the degree of pressure on reserve positions, an action expected to be associated with a small increase in short-term money market interest rates; the statement called it the first firming of reserve market conditions by the Committee since early 1989.

In August 1998 Russia suddenly devalued its currency and stopped payments on its debt; Long-Term Capital Management, a hedge fund betting that spreads in its portfolios would converge, saw them diverge and began seeking additional capital, and the Federal Reserve came to be concerned that a fire sale of its positions could potentially impair the economy. Trigger date not stated on the cited page.
source_title: Federal Reserve History: Near Failure of Long-Term Capital Management

description_en: On 26 November 2001 the NBER's Business Cycle Dating Committee determined that a peak in business activity occurred in the US economy in March 2001; a peak marks the end of an expansion and the beginning of a recession. Trigger date not stated on the cited page.
source_title: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee announcement, November 26, 2001

description_en: In 2007 losses on mortgage-related financial assets began to cause strains in global financial markets, and in December 2007 the US economy entered a recession; in the spring of 2008 Bear Stearns was acquired by JPMorgan Chase with the assistance of the Federal Reserve, and in September 2008 Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy. Trigger date not stated on the cited page.
source_title: Federal Reserve History: The Great Recession and Its Aftermath

description_en: On 7 August 2011 the Governing Council of the ECB welcomed new measures announced by the governments of Italy and Spain and said the ECB will actively implement its Securities Markets Programme, designed to help restore a better transmission of its monetary policy decisions, taking account of dysfunctional market segments.
source_title: ECB: Statement by the President of the ECB, 7 August 2011

description_en: On 22 May 2013 Chairman Ben S. Bernanke told the Joint Economic Committee of the US Congress that the Federal Open Market Committee is prepared to increase or reduce the pace of its asset purchases as the outlook for the labor market or inflation changes.
source_title: Testimony by Chairman Bernanke on the economic outlook, May 22, 2013

description_en: On 11 March 2020 the Director-General of the World Health Organization said that WHO had made the assessment that COVID-19 can be characterized as a pandemic.
source_title: WHO Director-General's opening remarks at the media briefing on COVID-19, 11 March 2020
